+description: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
+---
+
+# Dedup local packs against the canon
+
+The **method** of the growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile a repo's own **local packs**
+(`.claudinite/local/packs/`; legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
+window) against the shared canon it consumes, pruning local items the canon now covers. Two
+callers share it: the unattended [growth-dedup task](../../tasks/growth-dedup/task.md) (which
+frames the run — dispatch, the human-gated PR, tracking issue), and an owner asking in-session
+to reconcile local packs against the canon. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine.
+
+**The yardstick is the mounted canon** — the exact revision the repo currently consumes, what
+`.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp — never a live fetch (a promotion is visible
+here only once baselining has converged the mount to include it). The mount is never a prune
+*target*, only what you prune *against*.
+
+## The three actions — every one removes portable text
+
+- **Remove** a now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for
+  portable rules.
+- **Strip** a *partially* covered item down to its residue — when an item's general half is now
+  canon-owned but it still carries a stronger point about a narrower case, **delete the portable
+  half in place and keep only the residue**. A strip is a **deletion that shrinks the entry**:
+  lead with the residual point (using the file's own `(canon)` tag convention if it has one),
+  never with a meta-line like "this rule is portable (canon)", and **never re-state the
+  now-canon rule, its fix, or which pack owns it** — carrying it is exactly what you are
+  removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item:
+  keep the pre-edit text instead.
+- **Rephrase** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed,
+  so the local packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording
+  drift; it never grows the entry and never re-imports canon prose.
+
+An edit that leaves an entry the same size or larger, re-quotes the now-canon rule, or names the
+owning pack's fix is a **corruption, not a dedup**. When in doubt about a kept item, leave it
+byte-for-byte unchanged rather than "reconcile" its wording. The `dedup-prune-integrity` check
+([dedup-integrity.mjs](../../dedup-integrity.mjs)) is the machine backstop: it reds the session
+when a dedup-labeled commit grows a local-pack prose file, or when any change adds a line that
+restates a canon rule.
+
+## The keep-test: says *more*, not merely says it more specifically
+
+Every local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test.
+Distinguish two cases:
+
+- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's
+  classes, files, or names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only
+  illustration: prune it.
+- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule
+  leaves out: a tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower
+  situation. Keep it.
+
+So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the
+general point, or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.
+
+## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose
+
+The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when
+a canon check *enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every
+session and CI pass. Consult the machine-readable rule catalog
+(`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`: id, severity, description,
+doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose corpus, and
+when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line.
+This cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the
+same rule — prune the local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd
+prune a duplicated prose line. The keep-test above is unchanged.
+
+## Discipline
+
+- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon
+  line (or the covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a
+  real local lesson.
+- **Write only inside the local packs.** A dedup run's whole surface is
+  `.claudinite/local/packs/`; the `growth-write-scope` check
+  ([growth-write-scope.mjs](../../growth-write-scope.mjs)) keys on the run's pinned
+  `Claudinite growth:` commit title and reds any touched path outside it.
+- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green
+  before delivering.

# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)

It lands its edits through a PR that **auto-merges once the repo's checks pass** (no human review — the PR is armed for auto-merge, so daily capture never piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.

You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding scope**: it names the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the window — that is the activity to mine; do not widen it.

> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and **arms auto-merge**: GitHub lands it once the repo's checks pass, with no review queue for daily lesson-capture to pile up in. - **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
- **GitHub access is MCP-native.** Reading issue/PR activity and updating the tracking issue go through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). > **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**

  what you are removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item: keep
  the pre-edit text instead.
- **Rephrases** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed, so the local
  packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording drift; it never grows the
  entry and never re-imports canon prose.

**Keep a local item only if it says *more* than the canon — not merely says it more specifically.** Every
local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test. Distinguish two cases:

- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's classes, files, or
  names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only illustration: prune it.
- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule leaves out: a
  tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower situation. Keep it.

So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the general point,
or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.

## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose

The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when a canon check
*enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every session and CI pass.
Consult the machine-readable rule catalog (`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`:
id, severity, description, doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose
corpus, and when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line. This
cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the same rule — prune the
local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd prune a duplicated prose line. The
keep-test above is unchanged: a local item that says *more* than the check detects (a stronger point about a
narrower case) stays.

- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon line (or the
  covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a real local lesson.

  deletes a real local lesson**, so — unlike [growth-extract](../growth-extract/task.md), whose additive edits

  none reds the repo's CI and blocks the merge.

## Tracking

The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:

> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Dedup**

Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number**. A run that finds no issue under
the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open, close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no
meaning, only the log does. Log each run that changed a doc as a **dated comment** — naming what was pruned and
the canon line that now covers it. A run that prunes nothing logs nothing.

## Run on a capable model

Proving the mounted canon genuinely covers a local item before pruning it — and telling "the canon now owns
this" from "the canon states this too generally, keep the local cut" — is a **judgment call**. A downgraded
model prunes a real lesson; the review PR is a backstop, but a wrongful prune is easy to wave through in
review, so don't lean on it. This task declares `agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.

  names the owning pack's fix is a **corruption, not a dedup** — the exact inverse of the job. When in doubt

# grow_with_claudinite

Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.

This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | canon changed, or the project's local packs changed (or weekly) | a PR against the repo's `main` |
| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via an auto-merging PR |
| `conversation-extract` ([tasks/conversation-extract/task.md](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md)) | after a substantive merge, or to run the retention prune | the repo's own local packs, plus the prune on the logs branch |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | daily (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |

A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).

## The conversation lifecycle — capture at merge, extract in a daily task, retention

The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions** — the conversation-side sibling of the
issues/PRs/commits extract above, replacing the old in-session post-merge lessons pass. The two
halves split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session transcript, so it runs
in-session at merge; **extraction** only reads the already-pushed logs, so it is an ordinary
scheduled task with `growth-extract`'s access model — the logs branch is *in the repo*,
so reading it, committing lessons to local packs, and pruning are plain local git on the working
tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the GitHub MCP tools.

1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
   Right after a merge lands:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
   net), and pushes one file per merge onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`** branch:
   `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`. **Delta-aware:** a
   session that merges twice pushes a second, disjoint file for the second merge's issue.
   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
2. **Fresh pass — the [conversation-extract](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md) scheduled task**
   (precondition: a substantive merge, or a logs branch with retention configured so the age-based
   prune still runs on a quiet repo; local git on the
   repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It applies
   [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md) (the method — friction signals and the
   measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and token usage), routes
   keepers into the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed,
   a **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the weekly full
   sweep guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).

Adoption asks only for the `retention_days` value (10 recommended) — nothing to schedule, since
extraction rides the fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.

## Rules

| Rule | Kind | What |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-config` | hardcoded ([config-check.mjs](config-check.mjs)) | entry config shape valid |

**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through an auto-merging PR. It writes only the
repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central
promote task's job.

## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)

Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
project's own content;
the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).

Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in the owning pack's `rules` (its
failure message carries the lesson), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack skill**, and only
what neither can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.

The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # engine-tests/ mirrors engine/'s inner structure (#385 — engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is, tests stay canon-side); each pack carries its own tests inside its tree, the home's local packs included.
        # nullglob: a location with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/*.test.mjs engine-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local_packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local_packs/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs)
          node --test "${tests[@]}"
      - name: Conformance sweep
        # The world sweep's home is the test/CI flow (not the Stop hook, which
        # carries only the work scope) — this canon repo models the pattern
        # bootstrap wires into consumers. World only: the work scope judges a
        # session's change and runs at that session's Stop hook, not here.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage (.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md)
        # is the one change bounded to packs/ + skills/ — an ordinary engine PR legitimately edits
        # checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix
        # (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR if a changed path strays.
        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/promote-scope.mjs

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # engine-tests/ mirrors engine/'s inner structure (#385 — engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is, tests stay canon-side); each pack carries its own tests inside its tree, the home's local packs included.
        # nullglob: a location with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/*.test.mjs engine-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/*.test.mjs packs-tests/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local_packs/*/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local_packs/*/skills/*/*.test.mjs)
          node --test "${tests[@]}"
      - name: Conformance sweep
        # The world sweep's home is the test/CI flow (not the Stop hook, which
        # carries only the work scope) — this canon repo models the pattern
        # bootstrap wires into consumers. World only: the work scope judges a
        # session's change and runs at that session's Stop hook, not here.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Growth write-surface gate
        # The repo-side growth runs (extract, dedup) are bounded to the repo's own
        # local packs. Unlike promote below, a growth run marks ITSELF — its pinned
        # "Claudinite growth:" commit subject — so the rule self-gates and this step
        # runs on every PR, exiting 0 in ~no time on a non-growth branch.
        run: node packs/grow_with_claudinite/growth-write-scope.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage (.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/tasks/growth-promote/task.md)
        # is the one change bounded to packs/ + skills/ — an ordinary engine PR legitimately edits
        # checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix

        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')

to #269 / #268. The core⟂pack independence guard (`checks/test/core-independence.test.mjs`) now blocks any *new* core→pack/skill coupling, but it ships green with the current couplings recorded in its **accept-map**. Shrinking that map to `{}` is the standing goal; this issue tracks the deferred entries ("the rest"). Each accept-map entry names its file and a reason — that's the living worklist; the items below group them.

### 1. SEEDING — the engine hardcodes default-seeded pack names
`checks/run.mjs` carries `const seeded = ['basics', 'grow_with_claudinite', 'tidy-repo'];`. The engine shouldn't know specific pack names. **Fix direction:** let a pack declare its own default-seed policy (e.g. `detect: null` + a `seededByDefault` flag) so bootstrap/`run.mjs` discover it structurally. Also touches `bootstrap.md`, which describes the same seeding by pack name.

### 2. RELEASE — chrome-extension-release infra hosted in core `.github/`
The reusable release workflows (`.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*.yml`) and the `read-release-config` action live in the core tree but exist solely for the `chrome-extension-release` pack. **Decide:** whether this plumbing should move to live behind the pack that owns it, or is legitimately shared canon CI.

### 3. DOC_CITES — engine/design docs naming packs/skills as examples (**the "skills — discuss later" set**)
`checks/DESIGN.md`, `extending.md`, `growth/*.md`, `README.md`, `consumer-safe-changes.md`, etc. cite specific packs/skills by name as illustrative examples (e.g. "per the `unattended-agents` skill", "e.g. the `tidy-repo` pack"). Not a runtime coupling — nothing breaks — but by the strict rule (not by name, not in comments) they still name content. **Decide the policy:** may an engine/design doc name a pack/skill as an example, or must it speak generically? This is the skills question deferred from #269.

### 4. SEED_MIGRATION — one-time seed migrations name their target pack (likely accept-forever)
`migrations/2026-07-12-tidy-repo-seed.mjs`, `migrations/2026-07-12-grow-with-claudinite-seed.mjs` necessarily name the single pack they seed, and self-retire once the fleet converges. Probably a permanent, reasoned accept rather than a fix — noted for completeness.

### Open design question — where the planner runs
The decoupled planner (`routines/fleet/plan.mjs`) currently runs **in the maintenance session** over the *accessible* fleet (matching "the planner should just go over all accessible repositories"). The alternative is a dedicated **core planner GitHub Action** with an account-spanning token. If the Action model is preferred, that's a contained follow-up (a workflow + token, independent of the sheepdog census).

---
Definition of done: the accept-map is `{}` (or only holds reasoned, permanent entries like SEED_MIGRATION), and the planner-host decision is recorded.

on the canon's **first** scheduler run (#394 Phase 2 cutover, [run 30199274381](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/30199274381)). The task itself worked perfectly; the gate behind it does not.

## The claim vs. the observation

`migrations-retire` is designed so an imperfect call is recoverable. From the design record:

> delivers any retirement as **one never-auto-merged PR the canon's own CI gates**, so an imperfect quiescence call at worst opens a reviewable PR rather than a destructive direct delete

The first run opened exactly that PR — #431, moving all six active records to `migrations-old/`. **It has zero check runs**, six minutes after creation and counting. For contrast, #424 (opened by a user token minutes earlier) had its check run inside a minute.

## Why

The canon already documents the cause, in its own prose:

> `packs/git-github/skills/git-github-advanced/SKILL.md:70` — **A push or PR made with the Actions `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not start another workflow**

`worker.mjs` opens the archive PR with `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN`, which the scheduler workflow supplies as `${{ github.token }}`. `ci.yml` triggers on `pull_request`. That event is never emitted, so the suite never runs. The rule is canon knowledge that the new task walked straight into.

## Why it matters more than a missing green tick

The archive is not inert. `migrationActive` stays active-only, so moving a record out of `active_migrations/` **ends check tolerance for its legacy shape**. Doing that for six records at once is precisely the change CI was supposed to prove safe. Right now the PR presents as "no checks — safe to merge once green", and green never arrives.

It also fires on the first run of any repo that cuts over with records past TTL, so it is not a canon-only quirk.

## Fix options

1. **Open the PR with a PAT instead of `github.token`.** A PAT-authored PR does emit `pull_request`. `FLEET_GITHUB_TOKEN` is already in the scheduler's env and is proven working (this same run's `growth-promote` resolved its member list through it). Cleanest, but couples a `self`-scoped task to a fleet secret — though `migrations-retire` is canon-only anyway, and the canon always holds that token.
2. **Have the worker dispatch the suite explicitly** after opening the PR — needs `workflow_dispatch` on `ci.yml`, which is currently `pull_request` + `push: main` only.
3. **Accept it and gate by hand** — document that a human must close/reopen the PR to trigger CI. Weakest; it silently relies on someone remembering.

Recommend (1).

## Meanwhile

#431 is open with no checks. Before merging it, run the suite against `claudinite/archive-migrations` locally, or close-and-reopen the PR under a user account to force CI.

input.body:
Owner request: make the growth-related tasks (extract, dedup) work as skills, and add a check-the-work that makes sure only files under `.claudinite/local/packs/` changed before merge.

Plan:
- Move each task's method into a pack skill (`skills/growth-extract/`, `skills/growth-dedup/`), following the prose-to-checks / prose-to-checks-sweep split: the task.md keeps only the unattended-run framing (dispatch, PR/auto-merge mechanics, tracking issue, model), the skill owns the method.
- Add a `growth-write-scope` work-scope check to `grow_with_claudinite`: when a branch carries a commit with the pinned `Claudinite growth:` subject prefix, every touched path (added/modified/deleted) must sit under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted). Blocking; self-gating on the commit prefix, so it also runs as a CLI gate in the canon repo's CI on every PR (invoked via a canon-curation entrypoint, since core CI must not name a specific pack — the barriers rule).
- Enforcement note: loading a skill loads only its instructions — the check is enforced by the engine (Stop hook work sweep everywhere the pack is active, plus the canon CI gate), independent of whether the run read the skill.

input.body:
Closes #491.

## What this does

**Tasks now work through skills.** Following the existing `prose-to-checks` (skill) / `prose-to-checks-sweep` (task) split:

- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md` — the capture method: the durable/reusable bar, dedupe against the corpus and check catalog, capture at the repo's own level, the local promotion ladder (check > pack skill > prose).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md` — the prune method: the mounted-canon yardstick, remove/strip/rephrase (every action removes portable text), the keep-test (says *more*, not merely more specifically), checks-count-as-coverage.
- Each `task.md` slims to the unattended-run framing (executor dispatch, Context scope, PR/auto-merge mechanics, tracking issue, model) and delegates the method: "The method lives in the skill." Skills are also invocable in-session for owner-requested capture/reconcile work.

**A write-surface check gates the runs.** New `growth-write-scope` (blocking, work scope, registered on `grow_with_claudinite`): both task docs now pin commit titles (`Claudinite growth: extract lessons` / `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`), and when a branch carries a `Claudinite growth:`-prefixed commit subject, every touched path — added, modified, or deleted — must sit under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window). Prose is the request; this post-hoc diff check is the guarantee, mirroring the promote stage's `promote-scope` gate.

It enforces at two points:
- **Session Stop hook** (work sweep) — everywhere the pack is active, consumers included: the unattended session can't finish cleanly with a stray path.
- **Canon CI, before merge** — a new self-gating step runs on every PR via `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs` (core CI must not name a specific pack — the barriers rule — so the home's local pack owns the invocation, exactly as `promote-scope` does; the step exits 0 in ~no time on non-growth branches).

**Behavioral tightening.** A usage-site gotcha previously could land as a source-file comment in the auto-merging extract PR — unreviewed edits to product source. Under the gate, an unattended run records the gotcha in the owning local pack *naming the site*; placing the comment itself is attended, human-reviewed work. The skills and task nevers state this.

## Supporting changes

- `engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs`: `Work` gains a `deleted` delegate (pure mechanism, like `changedFiles`) so the rule can scope deletions.
- `dedup-prune-integrity`'s `doc` pointer follows the strip discipline into the `growth-dedup` skill.
- Pack README: a Skills section naming everything the pack bundles, and the Rules table now lists `dedup-prune-integrity` (previously missing) and `growth-write-scope`.
- Fixture tests (red-first: violating fixtures must find, clean ones must not) in `packs-tests/grow_with_claudinite/pack.test.mjs`: stray file flagged, stray deletion flagged, all-inside passes (both roots, in-surface deletions), ordinary branches ungated, subject-position-only prefix match, silent on the default branch.

## Verification

- Full suite as CI runs it: 720/720 pass.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking (7 pre-existing advisories on `main`, untouched).
- `check_the_work.mjs` on this branch: clean.
- CLI gate self-gates OK on a non-growth branch.

Done — [PR #492](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/492) is up (refs [#491](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/491)). Both growth tasks now work through skills, and a new `growth-write-scope` check certifies that a growth run touched nothing outside `.claudinite/local/packs/`.

**What landed**

- **Two new pack skills** — `skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md` (the capture bar, dedupe, the local promotion ladder) and `skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md` (remove/strip/rephrase, the keep-test, checks-count-as-coverage). Each `task.md` slimmed to the unattended framing and delegates with "The method lives in the skill" — the exact split the repo already uses for `prose-to-checks` (skill) vs `prose-to-checks-sweep` (task). The skills are also invocable in-session for owner-requested capture or reconcile work.
- **The write-surface check** — both tasks now pin commit titles (`Claudinite growth: extract lessons` / `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`), and the check keys on that `Claudinite growth:` subject prefix: when a branch carries such a commit, every added, modified, or deleted path must be under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (legacy `local_packs/` accepted). Blocking, with red-first fixture tests. It also runs as a self-gating CI step on every canon PR, invoked via `canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs` because core CI naming a specific pack trips the barriers check (same reason `promote-scope` lives there).

**Your two questions**

*Would this work as a task?* Yes — a task delegating its method to a skill is already the established pattern here, so nothing about the scheduler contracts (`task.mjs`) had to change.

*Does using the skill load the tests and run them before merge?* No — that causal chain isn't how enforcement works here, and that's actually the strength of the design. Loading a skill loads only its SKILL.md instructions into the agent's context — it's advice, and an agent that never reads it (or ignores it) is unconstrained by it. The check is enforced by the engine independently of skill loading: the pack registry picks it up because the pack is declared, and it runs at the session's **Stop hook** — the unattended run can't finish cleanly with a stray path, whether or not it read the skill. The fixture tests don't gate the growth PR at all; they run in the repo's test suite to prove the *check itself* works. As the repo's own checks DESIGN puts it: prose is a request; the post-hoc diff check is the guarantee.

One honest caveat on "before merge": the Stop hook is self-limiting (after blocking twice on identical findings it lets the session stop), and a consumer repo's CI runs only the world sweep — so for consumers the hard enforcement point is the session, not GitHub's merge gate. In the canon repo the new CI step *is* a hard pre-merge gate. If you later want the same hard gate in consumers, bootstrap would need to wire `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/growth-write-scope.mjs` into their CI — the CLI already supports it.

**One behavioral tightening worth your eyes on the PR:** extract's doc previously let a usage-site gotcha land as a source-code comment in the auto-merging PR — i.e., unreviewed edits to product source. The gate forbids that: an unattended run now records the gotcha in the owning local pack naming the site, and placing the comment is attended-only work. Also verified: 720/720 tests pass, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean.

> ⚠️ Still open: **PR #492 awaits your review** (the write-surface tightening above is the one judgment call to sanity-check). Optional follow-ups if you want them: extend the pinned commit convention to `conversation-extract` and `growth-discover-packs` so their auto-merge runs are gated too, and I can watch the PR for CI/review activity — just say the word.

---
name: growth-extract
description: Capture durable, reusable lessons from a repo's recent activity into its own local packs (.claudinite/local/packs/), routed down the local promotion ladder. Use when the growth extract task runs, or when the owner asks to capture lessons from recent repo work into its packs.
---

# Extract lessons into the repo's local packs

The **method** of the growth lifecycle's capture stage: mine a window of repo activity — commits,
PRs, issues — for durable lessons and fold them into the repo's own **local packs**
(`.claudinite/local/packs/`; the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
window). Two callers share it: the unattended daily
[growth-extract task](../../tasks/growth-extract/task.md) (which frames the run — window scope,
auto-merge PR, tracking issue), and an owner asking in-session to capture lessons from recent
repo work. Mining a *conversation* is different — its friction signals live in
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — but a keeper from either source routes
through the same ladder below.

## Capture at the repo's own level

Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files,
services, or mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear, but don't force either
extreme: don't contort a lesson to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general,
portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the central promote task's job, done canon-side later
(it picks up whatever is merged here by its next run); here, just capture it usefully and let
promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.

## The bar: durable, reusable, genuinely new

Extract only **durable, reusable lessons** — gotchas, engineering practices, test discipline,
architecture rules, project mechanics — and **dedupe** each against what the repo already
documents, its checks included (the rule catalog:
`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list` — in the canon repo itself,
`node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`). A lesson already covered, even worded
differently, even enforced by a check, is not a new lesson. When in doubt, leave it out — a
duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, and finding nothing is a
perfectly good outcome.

## Route each lesson down the local promotion ladder

Pick the local pack whose territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack;
some segregate a domain pack), then prefer the strongest mechanism:

1. **A deterministic rule becomes a check** in that pack's `rules` — author the `.mjs`, list it
   on the pack's `pack.mjs`, add a red-first fixture; its failure message *is* the lesson. A new
   check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one; a check that
   can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
2. **An activity-scoped procedure becomes a pack skill.**
3. **Only what neither can carry** lands as terse **prose** in the pack's `RULES.md`.

Write more checks and less prose; keep each addition terse and in the repo's own voice.

---
name: growth-dedup
description: Prune a repo's local packs of items the mounted Claudinite canon now covers — remove, strip to residue, or track a wording drift, never grow an entry. Use when the growth dedup task runs, or when asked to reconcile or dedup local packs against the canon.
---

# Dedup local packs against the canon

The **method** of the growth lifecycle's pruning stage: reconcile a repo's own **local packs**
(`.claudinite/local/packs/`; legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
window) against the shared canon it consumes, pruning local items the canon now covers. Two
callers share it: the unattended [growth-dedup task](../../tasks/growth-dedup/task.md) (which
frames the run — dispatch, the human-gated PR, tracking issue), and an owner asking in-session
to reconcile local packs against the canon. Often there's nothing to prune, and that's fine.

**The yardstick is the mounted canon** — the exact revision the repo currently consumes, what
`.claudinite/shared/` holds at the mount's stamp — never a live fetch (a promotion is visible
here only once baselining has converged the mount to include it). The mount is never a prune
*target*, only what you prune *against*.

## The three actions — every one removes portable text

- **Remove** a now-duplicated local item, since the canon is the single source of truth for
  portable rules.
- **Strip** a *partially* covered item down to its residue — when an item's general half is now
  canon-owned but it still carries a stronger point about a narrower case, **delete the portable
  half in place and keep only the residue**. A strip is a **deletion that shrinks the entry**:
  lead with the residual point (using the file's own `(canon)` tag convention if it has one),
  never with a meta-line like "this rule is portable (canon)", and **never re-state the
  now-canon rule, its fix, or which pack owns it** — carrying it is exactly what you are
  removing. If your "strip" adds words or restates the canon, you have *un*-deduped the item:
  keep the pre-edit text instead.
- **Rephrase** a local procedure *only* when the canon's wording of the same idea has changed,
  so the local packs stay consistent with the canon they point at — a rephrase tracks a wording
  drift; it never grows the entry and never re-imports canon prose.

An edit that leaves an entry the same size or larger, re-quotes the now-canon rule, or names the
owning pack's fix is a **corruption, not a dedup**. When in doubt about a kept item, leave it
byte-for-byte unchanged rather than "reconcile" its wording. The `dedup-prune-integrity` check
([dedup-integrity.mjs](../../dedup-integrity.mjs)) is the machine backstop: it reds the session
when a dedup-labeled commit grows a local-pack prose file, or when any change adds a line that
restates a canon rule.

## The keep-test: says *more*, not merely says it more specifically

Every local item is more specific than the canon, so specificity alone is never the test.
Distinguish two cases:

- **The general rule in local dress** — it makes the canon's point but leans on this repo's
  classes, files, or names to make it. Once the canon covers the point, those names were only
  illustration: prune it.
- **A stronger point about a narrower case** — it asserts something the canon's general rule
  leaves out: a tighter constraint, a sharper claim that holds for this repo's narrower
  situation. Keep it.

So ask not "is it specific" (it always is) but "does it only lean on specific names to make the
general point, or does it make a point the canon doesn't?" Prune the first; keep the second.

## A canon check covers an item too — and more strongly than prose

The canon carries rules as **conformance checks**, not only prose. A local item is covered when
a canon check *enforces* it — stronger coverage than a stated line, since the rule runs on every
session and CI pass. Consult the machine-readable rule catalog
(`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`: id, severity, description,
doc pointer — it lists the active local packs' own checks too) alongside the prose corpus, and
when a check covers the item, **quote the rule id** where you'd otherwise quote a canon line.
This cuts both ways: a **local pack's own check** is redundant once a canon check enforces the
same rule — prune the local `.mjs` (and drop it from `pack.mjs` + its fixture) exactly as you'd
prune a duplicated prose line. The keep-test above is unchanged.

## Discipline

- **Only remove a local item you can show the mounted canon genuinely covers — quote the canon
  line (or the covering check's rule id).** When unsure, leave it; a wrongful prune deletes a
  real local lesson.
- **Write only inside the local packs.** A dedup run's whole surface is
  `.claudinite/local/packs/`; the `growth-write-scope` check
  ([growth-write-scope.mjs](../../growth-write-scope.mjs)) keys on the run's pinned
  `Claudinite growth:` commit title and reds any touched path outside it.
- If an edit touches something a test reads, run the repo's offline test suite and keep it green
  before delivering.

# grow_with_claudinite

Opt into the **growth lifecycle** — declaring this pack enrolls a repo in contributing its hard-won
lessons up to the shared Claudinite canon, and in pruning its local packs once the canon owns them.
Seeded by default (`--init` + the one-time `grow-with-claudinite-seed` baseline migration for the
existing fleet), and **opt-out by removal**: baselining never re-adds it.

This pack carries the **repo-side** stages of the growth lifecycle: capturing a repo's own
lessons into its local packs, and pruning them once the shared canon covers them. The central
**promote** stage — which lifts portable lessons up into the shared canon — is a home-only duty
that runs canon-side, not a repo-side task, so it lives outside this pack.

Its scheduled work is five tasks under this pack's own `tasks/`, each discovered by the repo's
scheduler (`engine/scheduler/discover.mjs`) wherever the pack is declared:

| Task | Runs when | Where it lands |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-extract` ([tasks/growth-extract/task.md](tasks/growth-extract/task.md)) | the project changed in the window | the repo's own local packs, via a PR that auto-merges after CI |
| `growth-dedup` ([tasks/growth-dedup/task.md](tasks/growth-dedup/task.md)) | canon changed, or the project's local packs changed (or weekly) | a PR against the repo's `main` |
| `growth-discover-packs` ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) | weekly | a new **local** pack in the repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`, via an auto-merging PR |
| `conversation-extract` ([tasks/conversation-extract/task.md](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md)) | after a substantive merge, or to run the retention prune | the repo's own local packs, plus the prune on the logs branch |
| `prose-to-checks-sweep` ([tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md](tasks/prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)) | daily (no-ops cheaply on a quiet corpus) | a PR converting always-testable pack prose into checks |

A member that wants the local stages without contributing lessons upstream **opts out of
promotion** on its own entry — `{ "id": "grow_with_claudinite", "config": { "promote": false } }`
— and the central promote stage skips it (absent or `true` = participate).

## The conversation lifecycle — capture at merge, extract in a daily task, retention

The pack also owns **extraction from working sessions** — the conversation-side sibling of the
issues/PRs/commits extract above, replacing the old in-session post-merge lessons pass. The two
halves split by what each needs: **capture** needs the live session transcript, so it runs
in-session at merge; **extraction** only reads the already-pushed logs, so it is an ordinary
scheduled task with `growth-extract`'s access model — the logs branch is *in the repo*,
so reading it, committing lessons to local packs, and pruning are plain local git on the working
tree; only posting the summary on the issue uses the GitHub MCP tools.

1. **Capture — a step in the merge-to-main skill** (in-session, where the transcript lives).
   Right after a merge lands:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo itself: `node packs/grow_with_claudinite/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`).
   Deterministic, seconds; it bundles the session transcript (sidechains inline, timestamp
   order), **scrubs enumeration-first** (every value the environment holds — `process.env`
   minus a short named allowlist of structural values, plus known credential stores — is
   redacted wherever it appears, with credential-shape patterns as the backstop; a secret the
   session itself transformed is beyond any static scrub, and push protection is the last
   net), and pushes one file per merge onto the orphan **`conversation-logs`** branch:
   `<stamp>--issue-<n>--<session>.jsonl`, commits marked `[skip ci]`. **Delta-aware:** a
   session that merges twice pushes a second, disjoint file for the second merge's issue.
   The branch is a **work queue, not an archive** — never merged; tips are cheap in shallow
   session clones and retention keeps them bounded.
2. **Fresh pass — the [conversation-extract](tasks/conversation-extract/task.md) scheduled task**
   (precondition: a substantive merge, or a logs branch with retention configured so the age-based
   prune still runs on a quiet repo; local git on the
   repo's working tree, MCP only for the issue comment). It applies
   [extracting-lessons.md](extracting-lessons.md) (the method — friction signals and the
   measured efficiency analysis, computable from the log's timestamps and token usage), routes
   keepers into the member's local packs, and posts on the worked issue, for each rule that landed,
   a **200-word-max** summary of the slice of conversation that caused it — the dialogue itself is
   never pasted there, it is far too verbose for an issue —
   **extraction is the only path to permanence**: a log that yields no rule gets no comment,
   and its conversation is gone once retention deletes it (a deliberate owner call).
3. **Final pass and deletion** — once a log ages past `config.retention_days`, the same task
   re-reads it with ~a week of hindsight (the rethink window), then deletes it (the weekly full
   sweep guarantees the prune runs even on a repo gone quiet). Every log gets exactly two
   judgment passes. **Unset retention = the prune deletes nothing** (capture-only, fail-safe).

Adoption asks only for the `retention_days` value (10 recommended) — nothing to schedule, since
extraction rides the fleet's one daily run like the other growth tasks.

## Skills

The methods the tasks (and in-session asks) run on:

- [**growth-extract**](skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md) — capture lessons from repo activity into
  the local packs, routed down the local promotion ladder; method of the `growth-extract` task.
- [**growth-dedup**](skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md) — prune local packs of items the mounted canon
  now covers (remove / strip / rephrase, never grow); method of the `growth-dedup` task.
- [**prose-to-checks**](skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) — convert always-testable standing prose
  into checks; method of the `prose-to-checks-sweep` task.
- [**generate-project-instructions**](skills/generate-project-instructions/SKILL.md) — decompose a
  project into pack facets and author its local packs.
- [**unattended-agents**](skills/unattended-agents/SKILL.md) — architecture and practices for
  unattended, automation-invoked agents.
- [**adopt-claudinite**](skills/adopt-claudinite/SKILL.md) — bootstrap Claudinite into a consuming
  repo.

## Rules

| Rule | Kind | What |
|---|---|---|
| `growth-config` | hardcoded ([config-check.mjs](config-check.mjs)) | entry config shape valid |
| `dedup-prune-integrity` | work-scope ([dedup-integrity.mjs](dedup-integrity.mjs)) | a dedup edit only removes portable text — never grows a local pack or re-imports a canon rule |
| `growth-write-scope` | work-scope ([growth-write-scope.mjs](growth-write-scope.mjs)) | a growth run (a `Claudinite growth:` commit) writes only the repo's own local packs |

**Pack discovery** ([tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md](tasks/growth-discover-packs/task.md)) is
an ordinary weekly task on the repo's own scheduler. The repo runs the whole pipeline over
**itself**: manifest its stack, hold it against the canon packs already on its shelf and its own
existing local packs, and — for genuinely project-specific knowledge neither homes — author a new
**local** pack populated from its real usage, landed through an auto-merging PR. It writes only the
repo's own `.claudinite/local/packs/`; lifting a local pack up into the shared canon is the central
promote task's job.

## Identifying a project's capture surface: its local packs (the same way in every stage)

Every growth stage operates on a project's **local packs** — the tracked packs a repo keeps under
`.claudinite/local_packs/<pack>/` (prose in `RULES.md`, checks in the pack's `rules`, activity
procedures as the pack's skills, scheduled tasks under its `tasks/`). That subtree **is** the
project's own content;
the rest of `.claudinite/` is the **read-only mounted canon** and is never a capture, prune, or
promote target. So "a project's local packs" means precisely *everything under
`.claudinite/local_packs/`, and nothing else under `.claudinite/`*. This is the normalized capture
surface — a structural set the stages read the same way, not a `CLAUDE.md`-graph walk over stray
Markdown (a repo with no local packs yet simply has nothing to extract, dedup, or promote here; a
project adopts the structure via the `generate-project-instructions` skill).

Prefer the strongest mechanism the lesson allows — the **local promotion ladder**, applied at the
project's own level: a deterministic rule becomes a **check** in the owning pack's `rules` (its
failure message carries the lesson), an activity-scoped procedure becomes a **pack skill**, and only
what neither can carry lands as **prose** in a pack's `RULES.md`. A check relieves every session's
context completely where prose only relocates it, so capture writes *more checks and less prose*.

The stages differ only in *how they read that set*, never in *which set it is*: extract and dedup
run against the member repo and read the local packs from the working tree; promote runs centrally
and reads the same subtree over the GitHub API (get-file-contents under `.claudinite/local_packs/`).
Extract writes into it, promote reads from it, dedup prunes within it — all against the identical,
`.claudinite/local_packs/`-rooted set.

Closes #491.

## What this does

**Tasks now work through skills.** Following the existing `prose-to-checks` (skill) / `prose-to-checks-sweep` (task) split:

- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md` — the capture method: the durable/reusable bar, dedupe against the corpus and check catalog, capture at the repo's own level, the local promotion ladder (check > pack skill > prose).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md` — the prune method: the mounted-canon yardstick, remove/strip/rephrase (every action removes portable text), the keep-test (says *more*, not merely more specifically), checks-count-as-coverage.
- Each `task.md` slims to the unattended-run framing (executor dispatch, Context scope, PR/auto-merge mechanics, tracking issue, model) and delegates the method: "The method lives in the skill." Skills are also invocable in-session for owner-requested capture/reconcile work.

**A write-surface check gates the runs.** New `growth-write-scope` (blocking, work scope, registered on `grow_with_claudinite`): both task docs now pin commit titles (`Claudinite growth: extract lessons` / `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`), and when a branch carries a `Claudinite growth:`-prefixed commit subject, the change must fit the growth write surface:

- **Under `.claudinite/local/packs/`** (legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted): anything — the local packs are the capture surface.
- **Everywhere else: only whole comment lines inserted into existing files** — the usage-site gotcha extract's method mandates (owner call: unattended runs keep placing comments right at the call site). Verified per file type (C-like, hash, SQL/Lua-dash, and XML/HTML/Markdown comment syntaxes; fail-closed on types the gate can't verify), via a pure-insertion subsequence walk: no rewritten or removed lines, no new files, no deletions. A pure comment insertion cannot change behavior, which is what keeps the auto-merging, unreviewed PR safe.

Prose is the request; this post-hoc diff check is the guarantee, mirroring the promote stage's `promote-scope` gate. It enforces at two points:
- **Session Stop hook** (work sweep) — everywhere the pack is active, consumers included: the unattended session can't finish cleanly outside the surface.
- **Canon CI, before merge** — a self-gating step on every PR via `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs` (core CI must not name a specific pack — the barriers rule — so the home's local pack owns the invocation, exactly as `promote-scope` does; the step exits 0 in ~no time on non-growth branches).

## Supporting changes

- `engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs`: `Work` gains a `deleted` delegate (pure mechanism, like `changedFiles`) so the rule can scope deletions.
- `dedup-prune-integrity`'s `doc` pointer follows the strip discipline into the `growth-dedup` skill.
- Pack README: a Skills section naming everything the pack bundles, and the Rules table now lists `dedup-prune-integrity` (previously missing) and `growth-write-scope`.
- Fixture tests (red-first: violating fixtures must find, clean ones must not) in `packs-tests/grow_with_claudinite/pack.test.mjs`: comment insertions pass (line, block, and HTML comment forms; both pack roots; in-surface deletions), while a rewritten line (comment appended to existing code), a non-comment insertion, a new outside file, an unverifiable file type, an outside deletion each find; ordinary branches ungated; the `Claudinite growth:` prefix counts only at the commit subject; silent on the default branch.

## Verification

- Full suite as CI runs it: 722/722 pass.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking (7 pre-existing advisories on `main`, untouched).
- `check_the_work.mjs` on this branch: clean.

Done and pushed to [PR #492](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/492) (description updated). The check is **not** redundant — it's arguably more valuable now, so I kept it with a widened surface:

- **Under `.claudinite/local/packs/`**: anything goes, as before.
- **Everywhere else**: a growth run may **insert whole comment lines into existing files** — exactly the usage-site gotcha placement you want. What it still forbids out there: rewriting or removing existing lines (including appending a trailing comment to a code line — the comment must be its own line), creating new files, and deleting anything.

The reasoning for keeping it: "only local packs changed" was never the real safety property — "the auto-merged, unreviewed PR cannot change behavior" is. A pure comment insertion preserves behavior; inserted *code* doesn't. So the check now verifies precisely that: a subsequence walk proves the outside diff is insertion-only, and each inserted line must be a comment for the file's type (C-like `//`/`/* */`, hash, SQL/Lua `--`, and `<!-- -->` for HTML/XML/Markdown). New fixtures cover the pass cases (line, block, and HTML comments) and each violation kind (rewritten line, inserted code with its line number, new file, unverifiable type, outside deletion). Full suite 722/722 green, world sweep 0 blocking, work sweep clean, CLI gate self-gates OK.

> ⚠️ Still open: **PR #492 awaits your review.** Known edge worth knowing: a comment line inserted *inside* a multi-line string literal would pass the gate while technically changing a string's contents — line-level analysis can't see string context, so the gate is a strong backstop, not a proof. # Extract lessons into the repo's local packs

The **method** of the growth lifecycle's capture stage: mine a window of repo activity — commits,

through the same ladder below.

## Capture at the repo's own level

Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files,
services, or mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear, but don't force either
extreme: don't contort a lesson to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general,
portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the central promote task's job, done canon-side later
(it picks up whatever is merged here by its next run); here, just capture it usefully and let
promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.

## The bar: durable, reusable, genuinely new

architecture rules, project mechanics — and **dedupe** each against what the repo already
documents, its checks included (the rule catalog:
`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list` — in the canon repo itself,
`node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`). A lesson already covered, even worded
differently, even enforced by a check, is not a new lesson. When in doubt, leave it out — a
duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, and finding nothing is a
perfectly good outcome.

some segregate a domain pack), then prefer the strongest mechanism:

1. **A deterministic rule becomes a check** in that pack's `rules` — author the `.mjs`, list it
   on the pack's `pack.mjs`, add a red-first fixture; its failure message *is* the lesson. A new
   check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one; a check that
   can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
2. **An activity-scoped procedure becomes a pack skill.**
3. **Only what neither can carry** lands as terse **prose** in the pack's `RULES.md`.

Write more checks and less prose; keep each addition terse and in the repo's own voice.

## The write surface: local packs, nothing else

A growth run writes **only** under `.claudinite/local/packs/` — never the read-only mounted
canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`, and never the repo's product source. The run announces
itself with its pinned commit title (`Claudinite growth: …`), and the **`growth-write-scope`**
check ([growth-write-scope.mjs](../../growth-write-scope.mjs)) keys on that prefix to certify
the boundary: any touched path outside the local packs reds the run. The prose here is the
request; that post-hoc diff check is the guarantee.

This bounds the usage-site-comment rule from
[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md): a gotcha tied to one call site *wants* a
comment right at that site, but placing it edits product source — outside the unattended
surface, where the extract PR auto-merges with no human review. An unattended run records the
gotcha in the owning local pack **naming the site**; only an attended, human-reviewed change
places the comment itself.

test suite and keep it green before delivering.

+# Extract lessons into the repo's local packs
+
+The **method** of the growth lifecycle's capture stage: mine a window of repo activity — commits,
+PRs, issues — for durable lessons and fold them into the repo's own **local packs**
+(`.claudinite/local/packs/`; the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename

+repo work. Mining a *conversation* is different — its friction signals live in
+[extracting-lessons.md](../../extracting-lessons.md) — but a keeper from either source routes
+through the same ladder below.
+
+## Capture at the repo's own level
+
+Write each lesson at whatever level reads naturally for this repo — refer to its files,
+services, or mechanics wherever that's what makes the lesson clear, but don't force either
+extreme: don't contort a lesson to be hyper-specific, and don't polish it into a general,
+portable rule. Making a lesson portable is the central promote task's job, done canon-side later
+(it picks up whatever is merged here by its next run); here, just capture it usefully and let
+promotion lift whatever turns out to travel.
+
+## The bar: durable, reusable, genuinely new
+
+Extract only **durable, reusable lessons** — gotchas, engineering practices, test discipline,
+architecture rules, project mechanics — and **dedupe** each against what the repo already
+documents, its checks included (the rule catalog:
+`node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list` — in the canon repo itself,
+`node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs --list`). A lesson already covered, even worded
+differently, even enforced by a check, is not a new lesson. When in doubt, leave it out — a
+duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, and finding nothing is a
+perfectly good outcome.
+
+## Route each lesson down the local promotion ladder
+
+Pick the local pack whose territory the lesson belongs to (most repos have one general pack;
+some segregate a domain pack), then prefer the strongest mechanism:
+
+1. **A deterministic rule becomes a check** in that pack's `rules` — author the `.mjs`, list it
+   on the pack's `pack.mjs`, add a red-first fixture; its failure message *is* the lesson. A new

+   can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.
+2. **An activity-scoped procedure becomes a pack skill.**

input.body:
Closes #491.

## What this does

**Tasks now work through skills.** Following the existing `prose-to-checks` (skill) / `prose-to-checks-sweep` (task) split:

- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-extract/SKILL.md` — the capture method: the durable/reusable bar, dedupe against the corpus and check catalog, capture at the repo's own level, the local promotion ladder (check > pack skill > prose).
- `packs/grow_with_claudinite/skills/growth-dedup/SKILL.md` — the prune method: the mounted-canon yardstick, remove/strip/rephrase (every action removes portable text), the keep-test (says *more*, not merely more specifically), checks-count-as-coverage.
- Each `task.md` slims to the unattended-run framing (executor dispatch, Context scope, PR/auto-merge mechanics, tracking issue, model) and delegates the method: "The method lives in the skill." Skills are also invocable in-session for owner-requested capture/reconcile work.

**A write-surface check gates the runs.** New `growth-write-scope` (blocking, work scope, registered on `grow_with_claudinite`): both task docs pin commit titles (`Claudinite growth: extract lessons` / `Claudinite growth: dedup local packs`), and when a branch carries a `Claudinite growth:`-prefixed commit subject, **every touched path — added, modified, or deleted — must sit under `.claudinite/local/packs/`** (legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename window). Owner call: a growth run has one responsibility — improving the repo's packs with rules, checks, and skills — never the repo's codebase, comments included; a site-tied gotcha lands as the owning pack's entry naming the site. (An intermediate revision allowed comment-line insertions outside the packs; commits `a5027c2` / its revert record that exploration.)

Prose is the request; this post-hoc diff check is the guarantee, mirroring the promote stage's `promote-scope` gate. It enforces at two points:
- **Session Stop hook** (work sweep) — everywhere the pack is active, consumers included: the unattended session can't finish cleanly with a stray path.
- **Canon CI, before merge** — a self-gating step on every PR via `.claudinite/local/packs/canon-curation/growth-scope-gate.mjs` (core CI must not name a specific pack — the barriers rule — so the home's local pack owns the invocation, exactly as `promote-scope` does; the step exits 0 in ~no time on non-growth branches).

## Supporting changes

- `engine/checks/helpers/work.mjs`: `Work` gains a `deleted` delegate (pure mechanism, like `changedFiles`) so the rule can scope deletions.
- `dedup-prune-integrity`'s `doc` pointer follows the strip discipline into the `growth-dedup` skill.
- Pack README: a Skills section naming everything the pack bundles, and the Rules table now lists `dedup-prune-integrity` (previously missing) and `growth-write-scope`.
- Fixture tests (red-first: violating fixtures must find, clean ones must not) in `packs-tests/grow_with_claudinite/pack.test.mjs`: stray file flagged, stray deletion flagged, all-inside passes (both roots, in-surface deletions), ordinary branches ungated, the `Claudinite growth:` prefix counts only at the commit subject, silent on the default branch.

## Verification

- Full suite as CI runs it: 720/720 pass.
- `check_the_world.mjs`: 0 blocking (7 pre-existing advisories on `main`, untouched).
- `check_the_work.mjs` on this branch: clean.
- CLI gate self-gates OK on a non-growth branch.

No comment allowance, no per-language syntax table; the check is back to its simple, obviously-correct form (which also removes the multi-line-string edge case I flagged earlier).

content.content:
# Growth — extract lessons (per repo)

The growth lifecycle's capture stage, over **both** lesson sources in one run: the window's repo activity
(commits, merged PRs, issue discussion) and the conversation logs captured from working sessions. Each
durable, reusable lesson is folded into the repo's own **local packs** (`.claudinite/local/packs/` — the
normalized capture surface) at the repo's own level, without straining to generalize it. The run lands its
edits through a PR that **auto-merges once the repo's checks pass** (no human review — daily capture never
piles up as review requests); finding nothing to add on a given run is a perfectly good outcome.

You run under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue whose **Context section is binding
scope**: it names which halves are live, the substantive commit shas and the PRs/issues touched in the
window, and whether the retention prune is due. That is the work; do not widen it.

> This is the **unattended daily** capture. It writes only the repo's *own* local packs, so — **unlike** an
> owner-requested, in-session retrospective (which delivers a PR for a human to review) — it opens a PR and
> **arms auto-merge**: GitHub lands it once the repo's checks pass. The shared canon stays human-gated —
> lifting anything up into it is the central promote task's job (canon-side), and that PR waits for the owner.

## Conventions used in this doc

- **Default branch.** `main` stands for **this repository's default branch** — substitute whatever the repo uses.
- **Access split — local git for repo content, MCP for the issue/PR API.** The repo's own content is plain
  **local git** in the checkout: the commits, the `conversation-logs` branch and its files
  (`git fetch`/`show`/`rm`/`push`), and staging the lesson edits onto a branch. Reading issue/PR activity,
  opening the PR and arming its auto-merge, posting the exchange summaries and the tracking-issue log go
  through the session's **GitHub MCP tools** (`mcp__github__*`). The unattended run has no shell GitHub
  access — the shell reaches only a git-over-HTTPS proxy scoped to one repo, with no REST credential — so
  never reach for `gh`/`curl` or a cross-repo clone.
- **The repo's local packs.** The set identified in
  [this pack's README](../../README.md#identifying-a-projects-capture-surface-its-local-packs) — everything
  under `.claudinite/local/packs/` (the legacy `.claudinite/local_packs/` accepted during the rename
  window), the repo's own packs; never the read-only mounted canon elsewhere under `.claudinite/`.

## The run — two source skills, then the upgrade pass

The **method** for each source lives in its skill; this worker only frames the run around them. Don't
re-derive any of it here.

1. **Activity half — the [extract-from-activity](../../skills/extract-from-activity/SKILL.md) skill**, over
   exactly the commits, merged PRs and issues named in Context. **Skip this half entirely when Context says
   the activity half is not in scope** (a quiet repo whose only reason to run was the retention prune).
2. **Conversation half — the [extract-from-conversations](../../skills/extract-from-conversations/SKILL.md)
   skill**, over the repo's captured logs. `git fetch origin conversation-logs`, then list its files
   (`git ls-tree --name-only origin/conversation-logs`); no branch, or no `*.jsonl`, and this half is done.
   Give each log captured in the recent window a **fresh pass** (its filename carries the capture stamp;
   corpus dedup makes an overlapping re-read harmless, so err toward re-reading the last several days), and
   post the skill's provenance summary for each rule that actually lands.
3. **Retention prune**, when Context says it is due. Read `retention_days` from this repo's
   `.claudinite-checks.json` (the grow_with_claudinite entry's `config.retention_days`) — unset means this
   step is skipped entirely (capture-only adoption). For each log whose filename stamp is older than
   `retention_days` days: give it the **final hindsight pass** the skill describes (anything it still yields
   lands like any other keeper), then `git rm` it on the `conversation-logs` branch and push (commit message
   ending `[skip ci]`). The branch is never merged and its history is never rewritten — plain add/remove
   commits only. This push to the non-default logs branch is outside the outcome taxonomy (DESIGN §1).
4. **Upgrade pass — the [prose-to-checks](../../skills/prose-to-checks/SKILL.md) skill, over what *this run*
   just wrote.** Both halves route down the local promotion ladder as they go, but a lesson written as prose
   under time pressure is exactly where a convertible rule hides. So before opening the PR, take the prose
   this run added and ask the skill's questions of it: does it clear the working-rule gate, and does it
   constrain a static signature a check could observe? If yes, convert it now — author the rule module,
   register it in its pack's `pack.mjs`, prove it with a **see-it-fail** fixture, and apply the deletion
   test to the prose the check now stands beside. **Scope is this run's own additions only** — the standing
   prose backlog is the weekly [prose-to-checks-sweep](../prose-to-checks-sweep/task.md)'s job, and widening
   into it here would duplicate that task's work under an auto-merging PR.

If an edit touches something a test reads (a doc constant, a code path), run the repo's offline test suite
and keep it green before opening the PR.

## Output: one PR that auto-merges after CI

If the run found at least one genuinely new lesson, it lands **all** of it — both halves, plus any check the
upgrade pass produced — through a **single auto-merging PR**: one commit for the whole run on a
per-run-unique branch, not one per lesson and not one per half. Open the PR (title
`Claudinite growth: extract lessons`, its commit referencing the tracking issue so the `task-lifecycle` gate
passes) and **arm auto-merge**: GitHub squash-merges it once the repo's checks pass — no human review, so
daily lesson-capture never floods review requests, while every change still gets a PR trail and a CI gate.
Where the repo has no CI, GitHub lands it as soon as it's mergeable. This writes only the repo's *own* local
packs (not the shared canon). A run that finds nothing and opens nothing is fine — and common.

A new check must ship green — see it fail on a violating fixture, pass on a clean one — so CI stays green and
the PR can merge; a check that can't be made confident lands its lesson as prose instead, never a broken check.

## Tracking: log each run under the task's own issue

The task's standing log is the issue titled exactly, in this repo:

> **Claudinite tracker: Growth Extract**

Find it **by that exact title, never a fuzzy match or a hard-coded number** (a bare number can dangle, and it
differs per repo). A run that finds no issue under the exact title just creates one (closed). **Never open,
close, or reopen it** afterward — its state carries no meaning, only the log does. When a run adds a lesson,
converts one to a check, or prunes logs, log it as a **dated comment** — not a sub-issue — so the issue
accumulates a scrollable history, each entry naming **what happened and where**. A run that changed nothing
logs nothing. (A repo that still carries a closed `Claudinite tracker: Conversation Extract` issue from when
the halves were two tasks keeps it as history — never post to it, never reopen it.)

## Run on a capable model

Deciding whether a lesson is genuinely new and durable — and deduping it against what's already documented —
is a **judgment call**, not mechanical extraction. A downgraded model adds noise or restates what's there,
and **auto-merge means no human reviews the PR before it lands** — CI gates correctness, not whether a
"lesson" earns its keep — so the capable-model requirement matters all the more. This task declares
`agent_model: opus`; the executor dispatches its subagent there.

## What this task must never do

- **Never touch the shared canon** — this task writes only the repo's *own* local packs under
  `.claudinite/local/packs/`; everything else under `.claudinite/` is the read-only mount, and lifting a
  lesson up into the canon is the central promote task's job.
- **Never widen past the Context window** — the halves it declares live, the substantive commits and the
  touched PRs/issues named there are the scope; do not re-decide it. That includes the upgrade pass: this
  run's own additions, never the standing backlog.
- **Never merge `conversation-logs`** anywhere, and never rewrite its history — plain add and remove commits only.
- **Never paste the conversation onto an issue** — not raw JSONL, not a rendered transcript, not the turns
  themselves. Each landed rule gets one ≤200-word summary of the exchange behind it, and nothing more.
- **Never delete a log younger than retention, and never delete anything while `retention_days` is unset** —
  deletion is the ack that both passes happened.
- **Don't add noise** — a duplicate or hallucinated "lesson" is worse than adding nothing, the more so when
  its PR auto-merges with no human review to catch it.
